newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Puts sold on best performing FTSE shares.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Puts sold on best performing FTSE shares.

text.p: Put options were sold on Monday on some of the best performing stocks in the FTSE 100, dealers said.

They noted the sales of 200 January 950 puts in Shell Transport at 19p, 200 January 950 puts in Glaxo at 31p, 500 January 650 puts in Natwest at 13p, and 200 December 600 puts in Abbey National Banks at 16-1/2p.
"These stocks have had a good run and (sellers) want to collect the premium," said one dealer.

At 1333 GMT, shares in Shell were up 3p to 980-1/2, after setting a record at 982p earlier. Shares in Glaxo climbed 1-1/2p to 956-1/2p. Shares in Natwest and Abbey National were up 9p to 687p and up 5p to 611p, respectively.
Elsewhere, 200 February 600 puts were sold in Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation at 35p. The shares dipped 8p to 594-1/2p after rising as high as 606p, the best level in about 15 months.
P&O is set to release its first half results on Tuesday. Analysts expect the the company to post a pre-tax profit of 115.75 million stg, down from 131.9 million stg a year ago.

In other trading, dealers noted relatively heavy trading volume in FTSE 100 September calls at the 4,000 strike. That's less than than 25 points from the FTSE 100's current level, and the September options are due to expire on Friday.
"There's a lot of interest at that level. Based on past experience, I'd say there's the potential for fireworks on expiry," said another dealer.
"Open interest is skewed more toward out-of-the-money calls, so I'd say there's probably more potential for the upside," he added.
